assessment.headline: Day 28. Trump extends to April 6. 8 tankers cross Hormuz. But Russia is arming Iran and Israel is speed-running strikes.
assessment.body:
The extension to April 6 buys time but solves nothing. Iran calls the US proposal 'one-sided and unfair.' 8 Pakistani-flagged tankers crossing Hormuz is a positive signal — but pre-war was 130 ships/day. Iran's parliament is formalizing Hormuz toll fees into permanent law. The blockade architect (IRGC Navy chief Tangsiri) was killed but the mines and systems remain.

The proxy dimension is now explicit: EU accused Russia of providing intelligence and drones used to 'kill Americans.' Israel is racing to destroy as many arms factories as possible in 48 hours before a potential ceasefire — suggesting they believe a pause is imminent but want to maximize damage first. The US has destroyed 2/3 of Iran's missile and drone production.

For India: An Indian tanker captain was granted Hormuz passage but warned 'conditions depend on too many parties.' OECD raised global inflation forecast by 1.2% because of the war. FII outflow ₹88,180 Cr in March. ₹44L+ Cr destroyed. The April 6 deadline gives India more breathing room but the fundamental crisis remains — LPG 10 days stock, petrol frozen, OMCs bleeding, Hormuz effectively closed.

The best-case scenario: Pakistan-mediated talks produce a framework by April 6. Oil drops to $80. Sensex rallies 10%+. The worst case: talks fail, power plant strikes begin April 7, Iran mines the Gulf, and India faces the worst energy crisis in its history.
